clue.text: Tools despotic captain put aboard?

parts.note: a tyrannical skipper drives his sailors hard; such men set inside SS (a steamship) would be the turning tools

explanation.surface: A tyrannical ship's master has brought his own equipment on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as S-CREW DRIVER-S: a bully who drives the crew, placed within SS, the usual abbreviation for a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hand implements with a blade for turning slotted fasteners.

clue.text: Something golden, we hear? Impossible!

parts.note: the proverb says speech is silver but its opposite is golden, and in that state nothing at all can be heard

explanation.surface: Someone doubts a rumour that something is made of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb calls quietness golden, and total quiet means hearing is impossible.

clue.text: Find new way for engineers twice at fault inside

indicators.note: inside says the fault word goes within the doubled engineers
twice says the engineers' abbreviation is written two times in a row

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
out means wrong or mistaken, as in a calculation that is out

explanation.surface: Army engineers repeatedly at fault have to find another route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles the engineers' abbreviation; 'inside' then sets the fault word within the second copy, before its final E. RE is a stock crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To send something by a different path is to find it another way.

clue.text: Wed, at length, when Grundy was

definitions.meaning: Wed is the short form of the day's name, so written out in full it is the whole weekday
in the nursery rhyme Solomon Grundy was 'married on' this day, so wed here also means married

explanation.surface: A note that someone got married, and when, in long form.
explanation.walkthrough: Solomon Grundy is a nursery rhyme: born on Monday, christened on Tuesday, married on Wednesday, and so on through the week.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation Wed stands for this midweek day, and the rhyme's Grundy married then.

clue.text: They may contribute to bouquet in wines

definitions.meaning: flowers often gathered into a bunch for a bride or a vase
pink wines, the French rosé in the plural

explanation.surface: A wine taster mentions what gives the wines their aroma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' looks like a wine's aroma, matching 'wines', but it is a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A florist's bunch often contains these flowers, and rosé wines are pink ones.

clue.text: Classic no trump slam takes a long time

parts.note: vint is a Russian card game, a forerunner of bridge in which no-trump contracts and slams are played
an age is a very long period

explanation.surface: A bridge player bidding a grand slam without trumps takes ages over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link joining the two pieces. Vint is an old Russian card game like bridge, here clued by its bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something classic is of enduring high quality, as a vintage car or wine is.

clue.text: Valley of R. Don had shifted

indicators.note: shifted says the letters of the preceding words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A river map shows the Don has moved away from a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' rearranges RDONHAD. The Rhondda is a former coal-mining valley in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhondda is a well-known Welsh valley, formerly a coal-mining district.

clue.text: Such broody females are particularly vulnerable

definitions.meaning: female birds sitting on eggs to hatch them

explanation.surface: A farmer observes that brooding hens and ducks are at special risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks sitting on a nest are broody birds, and the idiom names easy targets.

clue.text: Unmannerly king lying in sick bay

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: lying in says the king's letter rests inside the bed, just as a patient lies in one

parts.note: a sick bay is a ward of beds, so bay suggests a bed
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A rude monarch is laid up in the infirmary.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone badly brought up lacks manners, hence rude or uncouth.

clue.text: One's going to enjoy this demonstration of affection

definitions.text: One's going to enjoy this demonstration of affection

parts.words: One's going to enjoy this demonstration of affection
parts.note: a person about to leave is the one who gets a farewell party from friends

explanation.surface: Someone predicts a person will like a show of fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's going' reads as 'one is going to', future tense; it means one who is departing.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell gathering shows affection for a person who is departing.

clue.text: Absorbing stuff in world of antiquarian

parts.note: Thomas Fuller, the 17th-century English antiquarian and author of The Worthies of England
earth means the world

explanation.surface: Some absorbing material is found in the collector's realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'world of antiquarian' is read as the antiquarian's world, FULLER'S EARTH; 'Absorbing' looks like 'gripping' but means soaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: This clay soaks up grease and oil, used for cleaning cloth.

clue.text: Cut required by order of the crown?

definitions.text: Cut required by order of the crown?

parts.words: Cut required by order of the crown?
parts.note: a religious order requires its monks to shave the top of the head, the crown

explanation.surface: A trim demanded by royal command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order of the crown' suggests a royal decree; it is a monastic order and the crown of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks shave a patch of scalp as a sign of religious commitment.

clue.text: A couple of Georgia's neighbours gossip

parts.note: South Carolina (SC) borders the US state of Georgia
a couple of things are one plus another, so the joining word and
Alabama (AL) also borders the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: People next door to a woman called Georgia chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia is the US state; SC and AL are postal codes of two states on its borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Malicious talk and rumour about others is the stuff of tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Girl in family resort, as we hear from natives

indicators.note: local French speakers say the town's name as 'neece', so the sound is what natives would utter

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A girl at a family holiday resort, as locals tell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a female relative.

clue.text: Members of EEC depart to protest against something

indicators.note: the letters of the words are broken up as members, or parts, to be put back together differently

explanation.surface: Delegates leave the European Economic Community in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members of' signals that EECDEPART is split into parts and rearranged; 'to' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To disapprove of something is to express objection to it.

clue.text: Burning desire of party extremists to join Communist state

indicators.note: extremists here are the letters at the extremes, the first and last, of party

parts.note: Romania was a Communist state until 1989

explanation.surface: Fringe party members are keen to join a Communist country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' looks political, but takes P and Y, the first and last letters of 'party'.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive urge to set fires is a compulsion, literally a passion for flame.

clue.text: The blighter's in the navy

parts.note: a blighter is one who ruins or wrecks, and a wrecker of that kind is also a warship class

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the rascal has enlisted as a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blighter' reads as slang for a rogue, but here means one who blights, that is, ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast naval warship takes its name from one who wrecks things.

clue.text: Italian setting for Ransome's novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An Italian location chosen for a book by Arthur Ransome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by Ransome, the children's author, but means new; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanremo is a resort town on the Italian Riviera, so a place in that country.

clue.text: Bad driver had piggyback ride, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: had a ride on a pig is rode hog, a hog being a pig

explanation.surface: A careless motorist was once carried on someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piggyback' means carried on the back, but here literally a ride on a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish motorist who hogs the road drives inconsiderately.

clue.text: Hands prepared for action in mill

definitions.text: Hands prepared for action in mill

parts.words: Hands prepared for action in mill
parts.note: mill is slang for a boxing bout, so hands clenched ready to fight; hands also suggests mill workers

explanation.surface: Factory workers ready to start their shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' and 'mill' suggest workers in a factory; a mill is an old word for a fistfight.
explanation.definitionFit: Clenched hands are what a boxer brings to a fight.

clue.text: Very much love to include jazz piece in medley

indicators.note: to include says the jazz piece goes inside the preceding pieces

parts.note: far means very much, as in far better
love is zero in tennis, written O
a rag is a ragtime piece of music

explanation.surface: Much affection embraces a ragtime number in a musical medley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' means the distance word and the tennis zero together wrap around the ragtime piece; 'love' is zero because a love score in tennis is nil.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused mixture or hotchpotch is a jumble of things.

clue.text: Wrack and ruin for a daughter, we see

indicators.note: ruin says the following letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone sees destruction ahead for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrack and ruin' is a stock phrase, but 'Wrack' is the definition and 'ruin' scrambles ADWESEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrack is coarse brown algae cast up on the shore.

clue.text: Consider various views for painting, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a twin in sound

parts.note: an oil painting is a canvas

explanation.surface: An artist weighs up different scenes to paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various views' suggests landscapes; it means opinions, which are gathered by polling people.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to seek and weigh people's opinions, as in an election.

clue.text: Council to withdraw from heresy, no doubt

indicators.note: to withdraw from says letters are drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A church council sets about retreating from heresy, certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to withdraw from' looks like a church backing away from heresy; it pulls letters from 'heresy, no doubt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church clergy, a governing body.

clue.text: Sicilian port wine

definitions.meaning: a seaport on the west coast of Sicily
a fortified dessert wine made in that region

explanation.surface: A fortified wine from a harbour in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port wine' reads as one thing, but 'port' is a harbour and 'wine' the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is both a Sicilian harbour town and the fortified wine made there.

clue.text: King's son dropped off by railwayman

indicators.note: dropped off says the son is let go from the end of the railwayman's name

parts.note: George Stephenson was the pioneering railway engineer who built the Rocket
son is taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch's boy is given a lift by a train worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped off by' looks like a lift home; it means SON is removed from STEPHENSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen reigned as King of England from 1135 to 1154.

clue.text: Most accurate article coming out of E Mediterranean area

indicators.note: coming out of says the article leaves the region's name

parts.note: the Near East is the region around the eastern Mediterranean
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A precise piece of writing emerges from the Levant.
explanation.definitionFit: Closest to the truth means most precise, as in a guess.

clue.text: Unpolished type said to trump' card

indicators.note: said signals that the trumping word is to be spoken, giving a twin in sound

parts.note: to ruff is to trump in card games
a diamond is a playing card of that red suit

explanation.surface: A rough sort of person is said to play a trump card.
explanation.walkthrough: A rough diamond is a good-hearted person without refined manners.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncut gem is unpolished, and so is a kindly but uncouth person.
